sam: Heads-up: after the 8421 merge the staged rollout (10% -> 30%) hit a perf regression on canaries, p95 up ~28% and tail latency spikes. noticed during the night window. https://ci.internal/perf/8421-run

marta: ugh. which path? kernel selection or batching?

sam: early signal points to kernel auto-select falling back to generic kernels for short sequences. also batching smoothing flag was flipped in the PR. KV miss rate increased ~3% which amplified tail. attaching quick profile.

ryan: can you paste the profiler snippet?

sam: ```
thread: runtime/main
op: decode_token
old-kernel: auto-kernel-v2 (avg 2.1ms)
new-kernel: fallback-generic (avg 3.8ms)
batch-size-mean: 4.2 -> 1.9
kv-miss-rate: 0.042 -> 0.071
p95: 190ms -> 245ms
```

tera: that batch-size collapse + worse kernel = compounding. 8421 changed kernel heuristic to prefer memory-conservative kernels for >seq128. maybe the seq distribution shifted.

kai: CI perf job for that branch passed though?

sam: CI smoke (small run) passed but our canary load is more bursty. CI perf-run had p95 within threshold but the nightly long-tail harness caught it. link: https://ci.internal/runs/8421-longtail

infra-bot: Deploy monitor: rollout paused automatically at 30% due to SLO guard (p95 increase >20%).

marta: good the pause happened. who started a bisect?

ryan: I started a narrow bisect to isolate the commit in the PR that toggled `batch_smoothing=false`. early suspect: commit 8421b2 (kernel heuristic tweak) vs 8421c4 (batching tweak).

sam: ran `git bisect run ./perf-smoke --target p95` — pointed to 8421c4 (batch smoothing off) as the primary delta for batching collapse. but kernel selection also influenced fallback heuristics when batch < 2.

tera: reproduce locally with stress-profile: `./perf-smoke --seq-dist short --concurrency 80 --duration 600s` shows the same p95 bump.

kai: ops-bot, did the auto-rollback trigger?

ops-bot: Auto-rollback disabled for staged rollouts by default. Current policy: pause at threshold, alert on-call. Manual rollback required. See /policies/rollouts.md

marta: I think we should enable auto-rollback for perf regressions >25% p95 for canaries (prod-tier), but only if CI perf test + canary agree. otherwise risk flapping.

ryan: proposal: change guardrail to two-stage gating: 1) CI perf runs must stay within 10% delta p95, 2) Canaries auto-pause at 15% and auto-rollback at 30% sustained over 3 minutes. Also add KV-miss delta as a secondary signal (+3% absolute).

sam: +1 but we need to avoid false positives from traffic shifts. maybe use normalized p95 (baseline-model-adjusted) and require monotonic increase across two contiguous windows.

tera: operational checklist to unblock: revert 8421c4 (batching tweak) from the staged rollout (manual rollback at 30%), then re-run canary with batch_smoothing=true and kernel-hint=prefer-speed for short seqs.

kai: I can push manual rollback now. tagging on-call (marta).

marta: on it. initiating rollback to previous release. will monitor telemetry and post logs.

infra-bot: Rollback action: version v3.14.5 reinstated -> success (timestamp 1892345732).

sam: after rollback p95 back to baseline within 8 minutes. KV-miss back to 0.043.

marta: follow-ups: 1) tighten pre-merge perf gate to include a short long-tail harness that simulates bursty traffic, 2) add a canary-only probe that measures kernel-selection distribution and batch-size histogram, 3) consider enabling auto-rollback for prod-tier with cooldown window and jitter.

ryan: I'll open a small RFC + change to rollout guardrails and add the perf-harness to CI (PR incoming). also adding metric `kernel_selection.count` and `batch.size.hist` to canary dashboards.

tera: also add a unit test for batch smoothing flag so it can't be flipped without perf sign-off.

marta: thanks. great quick recovery. leaving this thread for the incident doc. next steps in #postmortems once we have the numbers. :thumbsup:

sam: attaching quick perf artifacts to the incident ticket: https://incidents/internal/INC-2026-1892

kai: ct: I saved the git bisect log, DMing it to the authors.

ryan: PR for guardrail changes: https://phabricator/internal/D3333 (draft).

marta: closing the rollout incident. if anyone sees regressions ping me directly.

sam: thanks all.
